narrative:
The model predicts you have a 79% chance of leaving your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to move on from the organization soon.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, having received other job opportunities while working here pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have not received such offers, so this factor made your situation look quite different from those who remain long-term.

Second, your overall experience of 6-10 years across all jobs also contributed noticeably toward predicting you would leave. While this level of experience is fairly common, it differs from the majority of employees predicted to stay, who more often have only 1-5 years of total experience.

Third, your 1-5 years with this current organization added further weight toward leaving. This tenure places you in a group where turnover risk appears higher compared to those the model expects to stay.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be at a career stage where external options and accumulated experience are making other opportunities more attractive. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore ways to increase your sense of long-term fit here. You may also want to reflect on whether your current path still aligns with what you want next. (248 words)
